title: HCLTech Surges Seven Percent as Strong Results Lift Indian IT Stocks
excerpt: HCLTech's September-quarter profit rose 21.2% and TCS gained 5.69%, as AI revenue, $3.26 billion in deal wins and a raised guidance floor lifted the Nifty IT index 3.12%.
body:
• HCLTech rose 7.11% to 1,306.80 rupees on 13 October after its September-quarter profit rose 21.2% year on year to 5,132 crore rupees.
  • TCS gained 5.69% to 2,248 rupees, Tech Mahindra rose 3.52% and Infosys rose 2.06%, lifting the Nifty IT index 3.12% by late morning.
  • HCLTech raised the floor of its FY27 revenue growth guidance to 2.5% from 1%, keeping the top end at 4%, and reported deal wins of $3.26 billion.
  • The Nifty IT index is still down 23% year to date, and investors are watching inflation at 5.54% and Brent crude above $100 a barrel.

Indian information technology stocks rallied on Tuesday, 13 October, after September-quarter results from HCLTech and Tata Consultancy Services came in stronger than a cautious market had expected. HCLTech was the top gainer, rising 7.11% to 1,306.80 rupees, while TCS gained 5.69% to 2,248 rupees, according to The Times of India. Around 10:55 a.m., the Nifty IT index was up 3.12% at 29,235.25, the Sensex was up 0.65% at 72,390.83 and the Nifty 50 was up 0.65% at 22,508.65.

The results trigger

HCLTech reported its results after market hours on Monday. Consolidated net profit rose 21.2% year on year to 5,132 crore rupees, from 4,235 crore rupees a year earlier, and rose 11% sequentially, according to DSIJ. Revenue from operations rose 11.5% year on year to 35,620 crore rupees and 3% sequentially. In constant-currency terms, revenue rose 2.6% year on year and 2.3% sequentially. The Times of India reported that TCS, which announced earnings last week, posted a 15% rise in net profit in its quarterly results.

Profitability also improved. HCLTech's EBIT margin reached 18.2%, up 131 basis points sequentially and 71 basis points year on year, which the company attributed to revenue growth, service mix and operating efficiencies. That margin print mattered because investors have been watching pricing pressure and AI-led productivity across the sector.

AI revenue and deal wins

Advanced AI revenue was the second driver. HCLTech put advanced AI revenue at $219 million for the quarter, up 78% year on year in constant-currency terms, taking annualised advanced AI revenue to about $876 million. Total contract value reached $3.258 billion, up 27% year on year and described as the company's strongest quarterly booking since September 2023. The quarter included a $1.14 billion deal with Mercedes-Benz. For investors trying to judge whether AI is a threat to traditional services or a new revenue line, those two numbers were the evidence they bought.

Guidance and the sector move

HCLTech raised the lower end of its FY27 revenue growth guidance to 2.5% from 1%, keeping the upper end at 4%, and kept services revenue growth guidance at 3% to 4%. EBIT margin guidance stayed at 17.5% to 18.5%. The rest of the sector followed: Tech Mahindra climbed 3.52% to 1,521.70 rupees and Infosys rose 2.06% to 1,038 rupees, while the BSE Focused IT index gained 3.04% to 35,366.87. The rupee strengthened to 95.25 against the dollar after the Reserve Bank of India announced additional measures to support the currency, adding to sentiment.

Dharmesh Kant, head of equity research at Cholamandalam Securities, told Reuters that results from Accenture, TCS and HCLTech suggest the worst of the sector's earnings growth concerns may be past, triggering value buying in beaten-down shares. That context is important: Tuesday's gains came after a weak year, not at record highs.

What to watch

The Nifty IT index has fallen 23% year to date amid moderating earnings growth and concern that AI will disrupt traditional software services, The Times of India reported. Two risks remain in view. Retail inflation accelerated to a higher-than-expected 5.54% in September, putting the Reserve Bank of India's rate decisions in focus. Brent crude futures fell more than 1% during the day but stayed above $100 a barrel, sustaining inflation worries alongside a weak monsoon. Global technology shares also faced pressure after reports of advances by Chinese chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies, with South Korea's Kospi falling 6%. The next test for the rally is whether Infosys and other peers confirm the same pattern of profit growth, AI revenue and deal bookings when they report.
